hook.line: Tomás has waited weeks for the plumber, and he finally shows up. English says "About time!" Spanish says it too, with a little more edge than *por fin*.
hook.en: About time you got here! (to a friend)

examples.en: It's high time you went to bed! (to a friend)

rule:
Say *ya era hora* when something finally happens and you are glad, but a bit cross it took so long.
*¡Ya era hora!* on its own: About time!
*¡Ya era hora de que...!* + a verb in the *-ra* past form (*llegaras*, *arreglaran*, *aprendiera*). The ending shows who did it.
No new person doing it? Skip *que*: *¡Ya era hora de descansar!*
Still waiting? *¡Ya es hora de que te vayas a dormir!*, with the present form (*vayas*).
smallPrint: Teachers call the *-ra* verb the imperfect subjunctive: a feeling about something that has happened takes the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *llegaras* or *llegar*, then type the whole sentence: ¡Ya era hora de que ___! (About time you got here, to a friend.)
yourTurn.why: A new person doing it needs *que* and the *-ra* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *arreglaran* or *arreglan*, then type the whole sentence: ¡Ya era hora de que ___ la calle! (About time they fixed the street!)
yourTurn.answer: ¡Ya era hora de que arreglaran la calle!
yourTurn.why: After *ya era hora de que* the verb takes the *-ra* past form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: About time!
yourTurn.why: On its own, *ya era hora* is the whole exclamation.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: About time Tomás learned to make black coffee!
yourTurn.answer: ¡Ya era hora de que Tomás aprendiera a hacer tinto!
yourTurn.why: *Tomás* is the new person, so *que* and the *-ra* form come in.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: It's high time you went to bed. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: ¡Ya es hora de que te vayas a dormir!
yourTurn.why: Still going on, so *es* and the present form *vayas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about *Vale*: *¡Ya era hora de que llegaras!* becomes: About time Vale got here!
yourTurn.answer: ¡Ya era hora de que Vale llegara!

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to a group: *¡Ya era hora de que llegaras!* becomes: About time you all got here!
accept: ¡Ya era hora de que ustedes llegaran!

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *ya era hora de que* the verb takes the *-ra* past form, not the plain present.
Almost. "About time" does not translate word by word; Spanish says *ya era hora*.
Almost. If no new person does it, drop *que* and use the infinitive.
